claims.text: The baseline material is a lightweight high-entropy alloy with density below 7 g/cm^3.
The intervention is addition of 0.1–0.5 wt% boron.
The alloy is to be mechanically alloyed and spark-plasma sintered with boron introduced as B4C nanoparticles.
Adding B4C nanoparticles under the proposed processing conditions will form a boron-rich grain-boundary phase.
The boron-rich grain-boundary phase will enhance grain-boundary cohesion.
The boron-rich grain-boundary phase will reduce oxygen diffusion along grain boundaries.
The boron-rich grain-boundary phase will reduce diffusion of corrosive species along grain boundaries.
Boron modification will refine the alloy grains.
Precipitation hardening associated with the modification will increase alloy strength.
The proposed grain-boundary phase, grain refinement, and precipitation hardening will improve toughness.
The boron-modified alloy will have higher room-temperature yield strength than the unmodified baseline.
The boron-modified alloy will have higher room-temperature ultimate tensile strength than the unmodified baseline.
The boron-modified alloy will have greater room-temperature elongation than the unmodified baseline.
The boron-modified alloy will have better saltwater corrosion resistance than the unmodified baseline.
The boron-modified alloy will have better oxidation resistance in air at 800°C than the unmodified baseline.
After boron modification, the alloy density will remain below 7 g/cm^3.
The hypothesis is intended to hold only if boron addition does not form brittle phases.
The hypothesis is intended to hold only if boron addition does not cause excessive grain growth.
The optimal boron concentration and processing conditions are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as having the same composition as the boron-modified alloy, even though the intervention changes composition by adding 0.1–0.5 wt% boron. The intended control is presumably the same parent composition and processing history except for the boron/B4C addition.
